text:
ConocoPhillips rose slightly today as crude oil prices held firm in a volatile energy market. Over the past two weeks, the stock surged 12.8%, riding a wave driven by geopolitical tensions in the Middle East—Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and shipping routes have pushed Brent crude above $109 per barrel, and those higher global oil prices support earnings for major producers like ConocoPhillips.

Today's modest gain reflects the broader strength in oil markets, even as traders showed some optimism about diplomatic progress in the Middle East. The $25-per-barrel gap between world oil prices ($126.55) and U.S. crude ($101.91) also matters for refiners and integrated producers: it signals strong global demand relative to U.S. supply, which can boost margins and international revenues.
